mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about a many‑one function f : A → B is incorrect?

options.A: Different elements of A may have the same image in B.
options.B: Every element of A has exactly one image in B.
options.C: No two distinct elements of A can have the same image in B.
options.D: The function can be onto or into.

mcqs.answer: No two distinct elements of A can have the same image in B.
mcqs.explanation: In a many‑one function, it is allowed that two or more distinct elements of the domain map to the same element of the codomain. Statement C describes a one‑one (injective) function, not a many‑one function, so it is the incorrect statement. Options A and B correctly describe properties of any function, and D is true because a many‑one function may be onto or into depending on the codomain.

mcqs.question: Let f: A → B where A = {1,2,3} and B = {a,b,c,d}. If f(1)=a, f(2)=b, f(3)=c, which statement is true?

options.C: f is one‑one but not into.

mcqs.explanation: An into function is one whose image does not cover the whole codomain. Here element d of B is never used as an image, so the function is not onto; it is into. The function is also one‑one, but the key property asked is that it is into, making option B correct. Options A and D are false because d is unmapped, and option C incorrectly claims that being one‑one excludes being into.

mcqs.question: Consider the functions f: ℝ → ℝ defined by f(x)=x² and g: ℝ → ℝ defined by g(x)=x³. Which comparison is correct?

options.A: Both f and g are onto.
options.B: f is onto but g is not.
options.C: g is onto but f is not.
options.D: Neither f nor g is onto.

mcqs.answer: g is onto but f is not.
mcqs.explanation: A function is onto (surjective) if every element of the codomain has a pre‑image. g(x)=x³ can produce any real number, so it is onto ℝ. f(x)=x² only yields non‑negative values, leaving negative numbers without pre‑images; therefore f is not onto. Hence option C correctly compares the two functions. Options A, B, and D are inaccurate based on this reasoning.

mcqs.question: Which of the following functions from A = {1,2,3} to B = {a,b,c} is bijective?
mcqs.explanation: A bijective function is both one‑one (injective) and onto (surjective). Option B maps each element of A to a distinct element of B and covers all elements of B, satisfying both conditions. Options A, C, and D fail injectivity (they map multiple domain elements to the same codomain element) and also fail surjectivity, so they are not bijective.

mcqs.question: A function f: A → B is called one‑one (injective) if:

options.A: Every element of B is the image of at least one element of A.
options.B: No two distinct elements of A have the same image in B.
options.C: Every element of A maps to a distinct element of B and some elements of B may be unmapped.
options.D: The function is both onto and many‑one.

mcqs.answer: No two distinct elements of A have the same image in B.
mcqs.explanation: Injectivity means that each element of the domain maps to a unique element of the codomain; i.e., distinct domain elements cannot share the same image. Option B states exactly this. Option A describes surjectivity, option C mixes injectivity with a statement about being into, and option D is contradictory.

mcqs.question: In a many‑one function f: A → B, which statement must be true?

options.A: Each element of A maps to a unique element of B.
options.B: At least two distinct elements of A have the same image in B.
options.C: Every element of B is an image of exactly one element of A.

mcqs.answer: At least two distinct elements of A have the same image in B.
mcqs.explanation: A many‑one function allows (and often requires) two or more distinct domain elements to share the same codomain element. Hence statement B is mandatory. Statement A describes a one‑one function, C describes a bijective (one‑one and onto) situation, and D is not required; a many‑one function can be onto or into.

mcqs.question: An 'into' function f: A → B is best described as:

options.A: A function where every element of B is the image of some element of A.
options.B: A function where at least one element of B is not an image of any element of A.
options.C: A function that is both one‑one and onto.
options.D: A function where each element of A maps to multiple elements of B.

mcqs.answer: A function where at least one element of B is not an image of any element of A.
mcqs.explanation: An into function is not onto; therefore at least one codomain element remains unmapped. Option B captures this definition. Option A defines an onto function, C combines injectivity and surjectivity (bijective), and D describes a relation, not a function.

mcqs.question: A teacher assigns each of the 5 students a distinct locker numbered 1 to 5. The assignment function from the set of students to lockers is:

options.A: Into, because some lockers may remain empty.
options.B: Onto, because every locker is assigned to a student.
options.C: Many‑one, because two students can share a locker.
options.D: Not a function, because a student can have more than one locker.

mcqs.answer: Onto, because every locker is assigned to a student.
mcqs.explanation: Since each of the five lockers is given to exactly one student, every element of the codomain (lockers) has a pre‑image, satisfying the definition of an onto (surjective) function. Option A is false because no locker is left empty, C is false because the assignment is one‑to‑one, and D is false because each student receives exactly one locker, satisfying the definition of a function.
